costNodePlain: Money set aside for loans that may not be repaid — the provision for credit losses: $2.6B of loans were charged off in the quarter and $810M was added to reserves.

opex.name: Compensation expense
opex.note: Pay and benefits for the bank's workforce — its biggest cost.

opex.name: Technology, communications & equipment
opex.note: Technology, telecoms and equipment as the bank invests in AI and its platforms.

opex.name: Occupancy & other expense
opex.note: Branches and offices ($1,420M of occupancy) plus other general costs ($1,803M).

follow100Note: JPMorgan reports revenue two ways: $46.4B reported (GAAP), used here, or $47.1B on a 'managed' basis that grosses up tax-exempt income. Net income is identical either way. The rows reconcile to the $100 total within a cent of rounding.
footerNote: JPMorgan headlines 'managed' revenue of $47.1B; this page uses reported (GAAP) revenue of $46.4B — the difference is a tax gross-up that does not change net income. For a bank, credit costs (the provision for credit losses) play the role of cost of revenue, and 'operating profit' here is income before income taxes.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: reported basis, vs a year ago

segments.name: Net interest income
segments.note: Interest earned on loans and securities, minus the interest paid on deposits and borrowings — the bank's core engine, up 2% as higher revolving card balances and wholesale deposits offset lower rates and deposit margin compression.

segments.name: Noninterest revenue
segments.note: Fees, trading and asset-management income — up 17%, with investment banking fees up 17% to $2.6B and asset management fees up 14%.

takeaways.text: Noninterest revenue rose 17% YoY to $22.5B — investment banking fees up 17% to $2.6B and asset management fees up 14% — while net interest income grew 2% to $24.0B on the reported basis.
takeaways.title: Fees and trading did the lifting

takeaways.text: Net income rose 12% YoY to $14.4B and EPS rose 16% to $5.07 — the bank kept 31 cents of profit out of every revenue dollar.
takeaways.title: Profit rose 12%

takeaways.text: Credit costs were $3.4B: $2.6B of loans were charged off and $810M was added to reserves, mostly in Consumer — a build, but smaller than the $1.0B added in the same quarter a year ago.
takeaways.title: Reserves built modestly

verdict: JPMorgan earned $14.4B as reported revenue rose 9% to $46.4B — fee and trading income jumped 17% — while credit costs of $3.4B stayed close to last year's level.
